about: Every field the community collector records or publishes, with its ISO/IEC 20889 attribute class (role) and where its subject published it (origin). observations/collect.py asks the uor-deidentification app for each field's technique before it records anything and applies exactly that technique; a field not listed here is never recorded. A pseudonym is HMAC-SHA-256 (FIPS 198-1) under the DISCORD_PSEUDONYM_KEY secret, which only the collection run holds; `pseudonym` gives its form. The vectors are RFC 4231 section 4, re-derived from the pinned RFC by `collect.py vectors <rfc4231.txt> --check`, and the collector checks Python's hmac against them before it uses the key.

forms.hex: HMAC-SHA-256(key, 'discord-user:' + sha256('discord:' + id)) in hex. The input is the digest the record held before the key existed, so that record is re-keyed without any Discord id.
forms.snowflake: The snowflake's 42 bits of milliseconds, which the record publishes anyway as discord.message.time, above the first 22 bits of HMAC-SHA-256(key, 'discord-snowflake:' + id) in place of Discord's worker, process and increment bits. Perceval's discord backend orders messages and pages by the integer snowflake, so the pseudonym keeps the order across milliseconds.

files.name: rfc4231.txt
files.standard: RFC 4231, Identifiers and Test Vectors for HMAC-SHA-224, HMAC-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-384, and HMAC-SHA-512

fields.why: A Discord user id finds the member's profile in any server they share.
The username and display name the member chose.
Discord's own flag that the account is software.
Any guild member who opens a message id sees its author.
When the member posted or edited; the metrics count by period.
Discord's message type, pinned flag and flags.
Discord's channel type, which names no member.
A thread opened from a message has that message's id, so it finds its owner.
The title the member gave the thread.
The Foundation's guild; it names no member.
A channel the guild's administrators made; it names no member.
The name the administrators gave a channel.
A reaction's count and emoji, which name no member.
The address the author wrote into public git commit metadata; the corpus keeps its sha256.
The login of a public GitHub account.
